scope: Sequential tests of owned virtual displays only. Raw probe has no encoder, transport, or receiver. Current source hashes identify reproduction code; they are not historical executable hashes for the earlier exploratory matrices.

findings.baseline60: Confirmed fixture presentation/compositor-path limitation: same 120 Hz display/filter/format exceeds 60 distinct image frames/s when source submission changes. Buffered source frame IDs predominantly advance by two; layer plus explicit transaction flush predominantly advances by one.
findings.remaining120Gap: Unresolved division among source scheduling, WindowServer composition, SCK delivery and transient encoder waiting. Existing clock values do not prove unique content presentation. No maximum-capacity claim.
findings.sourceClock: CG mode, NSScreen and measured CVDisplayLink agree on 120 Hz in 120 Hz cases.
findings.measurementControl: Disabling all pixel locking/marker reads leaves buffered complete-sample rate at 56.25 FPS vs 56 FPS with reads; no pixel-reader explanation for baseline 60.
findings.encoder: Actual HEVC 60 Mbps ultralow receives 92.46 complete samples/s with corrected original fixture; encoder output ~90.90/s in native stats, ~88.71/s on the independently timed Node window. 53 raw deferrals, zero VT drops; deferrals are not an exact discarded-frame count.
limits: Complete samples do not guarantee pixel-distinct content; uniqueFPS is derived from decoded frame IDs only when markerDecodingEnabled=true.
Renderer progress is lifetime cadence; capture measurements use warmup and shorter windows. Do not subtract their FPS as synchronized stage counters.
Virtual Metal drawables report only zero presentedTime in these tests; no direct presentation success/drop inference.
The initial heavy renderer did not establish source liveness; its rate is excluded.
CPU/GPU load and thread scheduling are uncontrolled; repeats have long outliers. These are diagnostics, not a sustained 120 FPS qualification.
Physical Android USB and receiver rendering were not exercised.

rawResults.excludedFromConclusions: Source heartbeat stopped and valid markers stayed at frame 181; pre-exit-status runner did not establish source health. Not evidence of capture capacity.

primarySources.note: Apple describes up to 120 FPS for continuously changing content on a 120 Hz source.
